algorithm_notes: Finite residual resultant x roots must be replayed on BOTH selected branches, against original equations/domains, and compared exactly as joint points. Matching x alone is insufficient.

A common support does not mean two selected branches overlap. On the overlap of their regular slabs, an exact checked common x sample plus common support incidence and equality can establish the same connected branch. Need an existing certified rational-interior selector; do not use a floating sample as proof.

Shared-component intersections with other branches occur at source projection events, hence branch endpoints. Check endpoints of BOTH selected domains as candidates; the mixed-contact test detects losing these during residual saturation.

For regular graph supports, cross sign is sign((F_x G_y-G_x F_y)*F_y*G_y), adjusted for both traversals and operand order. At component nodes use an exactly selected supporting factor/cofactor when certified; keep original polynomial as point authority.

If both selected arcs belong to H and grad H is nonzero, their tangent lines agree and cross is zero even at a vertical event. If the gradient vanishes and no local branch-sector proof exists, retain honest uncertainty; do not infer tangency from shared equation alone.
No code has been changed for this design. Reproduce positive missing tests on a separately attributed candidate before implementation, and preserve the original positive-parabola disjoint fixture.
